p.s: Sales tax, nexus and indirect taxes (US, VAT, GST)

p.t: A state can only require sales tax from you after you have a real link to it, called nexus. Usually that means passing that state's sales limit, called a threshold.
Charge sales tax only in states where you are registered and actually owe it.
Most new small stores need a tax form only in their home state at first. Check each state's rules before you sell into it.
Set up Shopify's tax settings only after you know where you owe tax. Ask a tax professional before you act.
Sales tax (the tax added to each sale) that you collect is not your money. Send it to the state or country that charged it.

Collect sales tax only where the law says you must. Pay it everywhere it applies.
Start with your home state. Sign up there and collect tax only on orders from there.
Check the exact rules with an accountant before you act, because they change and vary by place.
Nexus: which states require sales tax
p.s: Sales tax, nexus and indirect taxes (US, VAT, GST)

p.t: Sales tax nexus is a legal link between your business and a state.
It decides where you must **collect and remit (send to the state) sales tax**. It depends on your business activity and where your customers are.
Nexus is a link to another state that **obliges you to collect sales tax** there. An obligation is something the law requires you to do. A threshold is a sales limit that each state sets.
You get nexus by reaching that threshold. Having one customer in a state does not create it.
Nexus is created by too many local employees, office locations, or other significant business activities.

Consult your 3PL (a third-party logistics company that stores and ships your products) and a local tax specialist. Their goal is to avoid unintended tax liability (tax you owe without planning for it).

A business with a **physical presence in a state can have nexus there. Physical presence means an office, employees, or ownership in that state. You can have nexus there even below sales thresholds**.

Sales tax duties follow where your business entity (the legal company itself) has a **physical presence**.
Orders shipped into that state then **require tax collection**.
Competitors in no-sales-tax states may look cheaper to buyers in that state. This alone is **not a reason to stop advertising** there.
Sales tax is based on the **shipping address**, not the customer's billing address. Collect the tax for the state where the order is delivered.
Collect sales tax **only where you are legally required** to collect it. But pay it wherever it applies.
Services that claim to offer free sales tax either **pay it themselves** or operate in states where collection is not required.
Collect sales tax **only in states where you have crossed the nexus threshold**.
Sales tax you collect belongs to the state. So you **cannot keep tax you were never required to collect**.
Most states with no nexus require no collection. Competitors not collecting tax may **simply be below the threshold**.
Not charging sales tax in states where the store has no nexus **is normal for small online stores**. Customers in those states do not expect to pay it.
Sales tax obligations start **only when a store has nexus** in a state.
Nexus: which states require sales tax (continued)
p.s: Sales tax, nexus and indirect taxes (US, VAT, GST)

p.t: Sales tax is charged on orders shipped to a state if that state has sales tax. The charge applies to orders in the state where the business is **registered** (officially signed up with the state's tax office).
**Do not charge tax** in a state where the business has no registration or nexus.
A **sales tax certificate is the state's official sales tax registration. It gives you permission to collect tax there. If you hold one for one state, only that state's orders** need tax collection.
**Do not assume** your home state has no sales tax. The home state is the state where your business is based. Verify its current rules before you conclude you owe nothing.
**Check your business's tax obligations early**, before the first sales.
Sales tax or VAT rules depend on where the business is registered and where its customers are located. VAT (value-added tax) is a sales tax used in many countries outside the US.
Operating in many states creates sales tax nexus obligations. With nexus in 16 states, a business may need to track sales tax across all of them. **Review rules regularly**, because they change.

A business in one state **only needs to register for sales tax in another state if it has nexus there** (2024).
**Check nexus with an official resource** before registering.
This is general information, **not tax advice** (2024).
Sales tax is **usually charged only in the state where the business is located**, because thresholds in other states are high.
Some states have no sales tax. Sellers **below a state's threshold do not need to report or pay** there. Report means filing a form that lists your sales.
Federal income tax is the national tax on your profit. It is based on overall net profit, which is what remains after costs. It **does not require state-by-state registration**.
**Register for sales tax only in states where you have nexus**.
A non-US seller (a seller based outside the US) with third-party suppliers in other countries **usually does not have US nexus**.

That seller is unlikely to exceed the sales thresholds in the first years.
**Confirm this with a tax provider** for your situation.

Whether a non-US company must charge sales tax depends on **how the business is structured**.
**Confirm the setup with an accountant** before deciding.

Each state sets its own nexus rules. **Check them before charging tax** on orders shipped to that state (2023).
Advice from a tax professional **is needed before acting** (2023).
Economic nexus thresholds
p.s: Sales tax, nexus and indirect taxes (US, VAT, GST)

p.t:
**Core rule**
Economic nexus is a link based on your sales volume (how much you sell), not on your office or staff.
Once sales into a state cross that state's economic nexus threshold, you **must collect and remit sales tax** there.
Thresholds are set per state. They are usually based on revenue, which is the total money from your sales.

**Check the current figure for each state** where you ship before acting,.
**Track revenue by state each year** (2025).
Most early-stage (new) stores **do not reach nexus thresholds**. Still, **check the nexus levels as sales grow** (2023).
In most states, a business under **$100,000** in annual revenue has no nexus outside its home state. So it needs a sales tax certificate only in its home state (2023).
Thresholds are typically high. So most new sellers **need a certificate only in their home state**.

They **register elsewhere** when sales there reach that state's thresholds.
This usually happens **after several years of growth**.

Thresholds differ by state. **Only collect and report tax where you are obligated** to do so. Report means filing a form that lists your sales.

p.t:
The **200-transaction test** appears in,, and.
**New York uses a different transaction count** (100) together with a revenue threshold of $300,000.
The thresholds are approximate and change. **Check each state's current figure before acting**.
Current thresholds and nexus criteria per state are listed in the **resource sections of tax tools** (software that calculates and reports sales tax),,.
**Sales-volume-based nexus in a destination state:** the destination state is the state where the order is delivered.
The destination state's threshold is **checked against sales made into that state**, not only against the seller's home state.
For example, a seller in one state with customers in New York **compares its New York sales with New York's threshold**.

Out-of-state nexus (nexus in another state) is **usually based on sales volume into the other state**.
**Sales into other states are the key figure to track**.

A business address in the home state creates **primary nexus** there. Primary nexus is the strongest link, created by your main business address.
**Nexus notification procedure**
Shopify is the online store software you sell through.
1. **Wait for the sales tax liability notice** that Shopify sends for that state. A liability notice tells you that you owe tax there (2025).
2. **Obtain a sales tax certificate or permit** for that state. A permit is the same kind of state approval, named differently by some states.
3. **Configure the tax settings in Shopify** so orders shipping to that state are charged sales tax. To configure means to set up.
4. **Repeat these steps** for each state where you reach the threshold.
Home-State Collection
p.s: Sales tax, nexus and indirect taxes (US, VAT, GST)

p.t: **Collect sales tax in the state where the business is located**.
In the US, sales tax generally applies when a product is shipped to a customer in the state where your business is based.
You collect this tax from the customer. Then you **pass it on to your state**.
The state where your business is registered is where sales tax registration is **first needed** (2024).
**Charge sales tax only on orders shipping to a state** where the business holds a sales tax certificate. Charge only to addresses in that state (2024).

**Charge sales tax** on orders shipped to the state where the business is based.
**Check the rules for each state** where orders are delivered (2025).
**Do not absorb the tax** to compete with out-of-state stores. To absorb means to pay the tax yourself instead of charging it (2025).
**Below nexus thresholds in other states**, sales tax is charged on orders shipped to the state where the business is registered.

If the home state has sales tax, sales tax applies to orders shipped there.
If the home state has no sales tax, **this obligation does not apply**.

A business **may owe sales tax in its home state** for orders shipped there, even if the customer was not charged.
**Do not skip it** to offer discounts (2024).

This is general guidance, **not tax advice** (2024).
Collect sales tax **only in the state where the business has a physical presence or nexus**.
Sales tax is **shown at checkout** (the payment page), not on the product page. It depends on where the business is registered and where the customer is.

It **must not be hidden** from the customer.
Sales tax charged at checkout is collected for the government. It **does not reduce your margin** (the profit you keep per sale).

Your wholesale cost (what you pay your supplier) **stays the same**.
**Competitors pay the same tax**.
Advertising "no sales tax" is **allowed only if you are not collecting sales tax on that order** (2023).

If you collect sales tax in some states, **add a note** such as an asterisk (a star symbol) that explains the exception (2023).
**Specific states**

Texas is a state with **no income tax**. That point alone is used as an example in (2021).
However, Texas has a state sales tax and **requires a sales tax permit**.

p.t: A Texas-based store **must collect Texas sales tax** on Texas shipments (2025).
The two sources answer different questions. **No income tax does not remove the Texas sales tax duty**. A duty is a legal obligation.
Nevada **levies a statewide sales tax**. To levy means to charge.
A Nevada store should **check with the Nevada Department of Taxation** for a sales tax permit when a supplier asks for a resale ID.
A resale ID is a form that lets you buy without paying sales tax because you plan to resell the item.
Delaware was reported to have no state sales tax, but **this should be verified**.
An LLC (limited liability company, a common type of business that protects owners' personal money) based in Delaware that sells online **usually has no sales tax certificate to obtain there**.
A form stating the exemption (a legal exception) may exist (2024).
**Ask your company formation provider** about filing requirements, including any franchise tax (a yearly fee some states charge businesses).
Sales from Delaware into other states are **taxed only where nexus exists there** (2024).
Some US states have no sales tax. **Check the rules of the registration state** before applying for a certificate (2025).

In a state without sales tax, **search the state name with "sales tax exemption"** to see whether a form is needed.
In most cases, **no certificate is required**.

Maryland **requires a sales tax permit under its own rules**.
**Check your state's rules before you register**.
Illinois sales tax registration requires a **sales tax and use certificate**. You can request it from the state revenue department (the state's tax office) (2023).
It is **different from your individual 1099 tax form**. A 1099 is a US tax form for income paid to you as an individual (2023).
Federal income tax is based on overall net profit. It **does not require state-by-state registration**.
Multi-state sellers from Delaware or no-sales-tax states: the sales tax obligations that apply are **those tied to nexus in each destination state** (2024), (2024).
Sales tax certificates, permits and resale certificates
p.s: Sales tax, nexus and indirect taxes (US, VAT, GST)

p.t: **Certificate basics**
In the US, each state issues its own **seller's license** (state permission to sell taxable goods) or sales tax certificate.

**Search your state's name** with "seller's license" or "sales tax certificate".
**Sales tax permits are issued by each state**, not nationally.
Some states, such as California, **add extra sales tax**.
Check whether your state requires a permit by **searching your state name with "sales tax permit"** on your state government's website.

A sales tax certificate is also called a **reseller permit** in some states, such as California.
The name differs by state. **Use a resource that lists the local term for each state**.

A sales tax certificate is **required in the state where the business is located**.
It is advisable to **obtain it as the business grows**.

It can usually be obtained **online as a PDF** (a document file).
Sources differ on when to get the home-state certificate.
(2024) says **register at the start**.

(2020) says obtain it as the business grows.
Both agree that you **should not charge tax before you are registered** (2023).

A sales tax certificate is required in the state where the business operates.
Once you have economic nexus in another state, **you need a certificate there as well**.
The EIN (Employer Identification Number) is a federal ID number for your business.

You **usually do not need a sales tax certificate for every state until your sales volume becomes very large**.
**Check the tax training before registering** for each state.
When starting a US store, **register the business in the owner's home state** and obtain that state's sales tax certificate (2024).

**Do not set up nexus tax collection from day one.**
**Wait until you actually reach nexus** before enabling it (2023).

Sales tax should be collected **only in a state once the store is registered there**. This normally happens after nexus is created.
Charging tax before registration can create **legal risk** (2023).

**Process to check whether you need a certificate**
1. **Go to taxjar.com/states** (TaxJar is a company that offers sales tax software).

3. **Read the information** on the page about sales tax in that state.
4. **Click the link** that explains how to register for a sales tax permit. Every state page has this link.

5. **Follow the FAQs** (frequently asked questions) there to see whether you need a certificate and how to get one.
**Resale certificates**
**You do not need a resale certificate in every state** you ship to. A resale certificate is the same as a resale ID. It is a form that lets you buy goods tax-free to resell them.
Nexus forms only when you exceed your state's yearly revenue threshold, which varies by state (2024).
Most states require a resale certificate once you generate **approximately $100,000 in yearly revenue** in that state.
Check your specific state and any state where you ship substantially (2024).
A resale certificate is needed for a state outside the home state once sales into that state **exceed about $100,000 per year**.
Example: a business registered in New York **needs a New York certificate from the start**.
It needs a New Jersey certificate **once it sells over $100,000 per year into New Jersey** (2025).
If a supplier charges you sales tax but you have not reached the sales threshold (nexus) in that state, **provide your resale certificate**.

You **should not owe sales tax** (2024).
If a supplier charges sales tax on a purchase, **identify the state charging it**.

**Look up that state's minimum nexus threshold.**
**Send the supplier documentation** showing the threshold and your current sales in that state.

**Procedure for supplier-charged sales tax**
1. **Identify the state** that is charging the sales tax.
2. **Look up that state's minimum nexus threshold**.
3. **Send the supplier documentation** showing the threshold and your current sales in that state.
Shopify Tax Settings
p.s: Sales tax, nexus and indirect taxes (US, VAT, GST)

p.t: **Where settings are**
To set up taxes in Shopify, **go to Settings** in the bottom-left corner of the admin (the back office where you manage your store). Then open the Taxes section.
**Shopify's own documentation** covers the full steps (2024).
In Shopify admin, **go to Settings > Taxes** and select only the regions where you must collect tax. A region is a country or area with its own tax rules.

Tax will not be added for other regions **unless you enable it there** (2023).
Shopify's tax settings let you choose the regions where tax is charged.
If orders from a state carry no tax, **check these regional tax settings**, since the store may not be collecting tax there (2021).

Shopify charges sales tax using **two settings working together**.
The first is the **Charge taxes option** on each product.

The second is the **tax rules** set up in the Shopify admin taxes settings.
The product option alone **does not decide when and how much tax is charged** (2023).

Shopify's built-in sales tax **does not usually get charged automatically**.
The operator (you, the store owner) must **determine liability and register for tax**.
Shopify collects sales tax automatically once you configure the tax settings.
But Shopify **does not file the tax returns for you**. A tax return is the form you send to the state. Use a separate service if you want collection and filing handled.

Sources differ on whether Shopify collects automatically.
(2018) says it collects once configured.
(2022) says it usually does not charge automatically, and the operator must determine liability.
**Work from the liability analysis first**, then configure the settings.
Shopify Tax Settings (continued)
p.s: Sales tax, nexus and indirect taxes (US, VAT, GST)

p.t: Tax collection can be set up directly in Shopify or with an app (an add-on program) such as TaxJar. TaxJar can also file the taxes.
**Compare both options before choosing one**.
With **"Include or exclude tax based on your customer's country" enabled in Tax calculations, checkout uses the local tax rate of the buyer's country** rather than the store's own rate.

A tax rate is the percentage charged.
**Default tax values on products**
**Disable the default tax value** on new products, such as an included VAT of 20% or 21%, if you do not charge taxes. "Included" means the tax is already built into the price.
A shown tax **can cause visitors to leave checkout** (undated), (undated).
When creating a product in Shopify, check the tax setting and **disable the default VAT or tax-included option** if no tax is charged.

Otherwise, a default tax line such as 20% or 21% **appears at checkout** (a tax line is a row showing the tax amount),.
**Stage-by-stage defaults**
At the foundation stage (the first build phase), no tax entity needs to be configured. A tax entity is a tax setup record.
**Leave Settings > Taxes and duties at default**, which uses Shopify tax services with the default taxes for the countries you sell to (2026).

Taxes and duties for shipping are **not configured at the start**. They are handled in a later stage of the build.
Duties are import charges on goods entering a country.
Duties and import taxes, and taxes for each market (a country or region you sell to), are initially set to **"Not collecting."**

Shopify recommends **starting collection in every place you sell**.
**Make sure taxes and duties are accounted for** in all markets where you sell (2026).
Shopify Tax Settings (continued)

p.t:
Sources differ on defaults.
says to leave the foundation stage at default.
says Shopify recommends starting collection in every market.
Apply the default at foundation. Then **configure each market before selling into it**.

On the Shopify setup page, **ticking "This store is a registered business"** is relevant for tax purposes.
The address entered during setup **can be changed later**.

**Regions and shipping profiles**
Settings > Taxes **lists its tax regions from your shipping profiles** (the rules for how each product ships).
A destination (a place you ship to) **only appears there once it is part of a shipping zone** (an area you ship to).
To add a missing region, **add the destination in shipping settings first**.
If you do not sell to other countries, **you do not need to set up tax for the "Rest of world" region** in Taxes. Rest of world means all countries not on your list.
**Only regions where you have a tax obligation** need to be collected.

Shopify **calculates "Charge tax on shipping rates" automatically** for Canada, the European Union, and the United States.
The option **includes shipping in the tax calculation**.
On a tax region page in Settings > Taxes, the GST box (goods and services tax, a sales tax used in Canada and other countries) reads "You're not collecting GST" until you **select Collect GST**.

Below it, Tax overrides lets you set **custom tax rates**.
You can set them per product collection (a group of products) with **Add product override**.

Or set them per shipping destination with **Add shipping override**.
**Checking collected tax**

Shopify's tax report shows the tax your store has **actually collected**.
**Use it** to check collected amounts instead of estimating them.
Remitting Collected Tax
p.s: Sales tax, nexus and indirect taxes (US, VAT, GST)

p.t: Sales tax (the tax added to each sale) that a store collects is **not the store's money**.

The tax must be **remitted** (sent to the tax office) to the state where it was charged (2024).
Customers **cannot be asked** to pay a supplier's tax (2024).

The built-in system does **not work that way** (2024).
Sales tax must be **collected only where the law requires it**.
But it must be **paid wherever it applies**.

Shopify (the online store platform) does **not file returns** (send the tax reports) for you.
A **separate service** can handle filing and remitting for you if you want that.

TaxJar (a service that works out, files, and pays sales tax for you) **calculates** the tax.
TaxJar can **file the tax and remit** it to the state for you.
TaxJar also **tracks** tax and offers a library of resources on nexus (a link to a state that makes you owe its tax).

TaxJar can **automate** quarterly sales tax reporting (reports every three months) when it is set up through the account.
It is treated as an **industry standard** for this.
As of **January 2022**, TaxJar calculated sales tax for the US (United States), Canada, and VAT (value-added tax, used in the UK and EU).

It did **not file or report** those taxes for Canada or VAT.
Check the **current scope** before relying on it for filing.
Once you have a **nexus notification (an alert that you have nexus in a new state), apply the steps** in the nexus notification procedure above (2025).
1. **Register** for GST (Goods and Services Tax, Australia's sales tax).
2. **Lodge** (send in) a BAS (Business Activity Statement, a regular tax report) regularly.
3. **Remit** to the ATO (Australian Taxation Office) the difference between GST collected from customers and GST paid to suppliers.

p.s: Sales tax, nexus and indirect taxes (US, VAT, GST)

p.t:
For a Canadian seller, sales tax rates **differ by province** (a region of Canada, like a state).
Use the ecommerce business's own taxing rules.

**Check TaxJar's Canadian coverage** rather than relying on general statements.
Canadian sellers must check sales tax **per province**, because rates differ.

For example, Alberta's sales tax is **5 percent**.
Confirm province-level rules with TaxJar's Canadian coverage **instead of assuming one rate applies across Canada**.
A Canadian business shipping to US customers **does not charge US sales tax** (2023).
Canadian sellers who are not charging sales tax to US customers should **set their tax rates to zero** in Shopify and Merchant Center (Google's tool for sending product details) (2023).

This matches competitor prices in Google Shopping (Google's product listings) (2023).

Australia: GST
In Australia, a new business **does not have to register for GST until its revenue (money earned from sales) reaches $75,000**

or more in a single financial year (the 12-month accounting period).
Before that, it **does not have to charge GST** on sales.
GST registration is not required for a new business until revenue reaches **75,000 Australian dollars** in a single financial year.
A business already GST-registered under an existing structure may **continue as it is**.
GST registration only becomes mandatory once revenue in a single financial year reaches **$75,000**.
Revenue from several businesses under the same legal entity (one legal company) is **added together** toward this threshold.
A new business that has **not made any sales** does not need to register for GST yet.
Registration can be done later, either directly or with an accountant, **once it becomes relevant**.
In Australia you need at least an **ABN** (Australian Business Number, a national business ID) from the start.

GST registration is not required straight away for a sole trader (a business run by one person).
Registering early makes you **collect and remit GST on every sale**.
Obligations once registered
p.s: Sales tax, nexus and indirect taxes (US, VAT, GST)

p.t:
In Australia, once a business is registered for GST, it **must collect GST** on sales.
Not collecting it when registered is **illegal**.

In Australia, retail prices **must include tax**.
Shopify's setting "All prices include tax" must be ticked for this.
A business registered for GST should **add its ABN** under General settings (Add ABN).
This stops Shopify from charging GST on its own subscription invoices (Shopify's bills to you).

In the US, the equivalent federal number is the **EIN** (the US federal business tax number).
In Australia, Shopify charges **10% GST** on invoices.
Adding an ABN under **Settings > General** exempts invoices if you are GST registered.
For a store based in Australia, Shopify may show a **missing-tax notice** (a warning that tax details are missing).
A GST-registered merchant (a business registered for GST) should **enter an ABN** so that Shopify bills are exempt from GST.
For a store based in Australia, Shopify bills are **exempt from GST** if the business is GST registered and enters its ABN in the tax settings.
Without the ABN, the store will see a notice that tax information is missing.

1. **Go to Settings > Taxes** and open the Australia tax region (the Australia tax setup in Shopify).
2. **Click Set up**.

3. **Click Collect GST**.
4. **Enter your ABN**.
5. **Click GST**. Shopify then collects **10% GST** on each order.

6. Under **Tax calculations** (the settings area for how tax is worked out), tick "All prices include tax".
7. **Click Save**.

1. **Register** for GST.
2. **Lodge** a BAS regularly.

Singapore GST on ad spend
p.s: Sales tax, nexus and indirect taxes (US, VAT, GST)

p.t: Singapore GST (Singapore's version of GST) equals **9%** of the spend converted into SGD (Singapore dollars) (2026).

The example used $100k USD and gave **S$9,000** in GST (2026).
At about **S$1.30 per USD**, $100k is about S$130k (2026).

At that rate, the GST would be about **S$11,700** (2026).
**Verify the conversion** before budgeting (2026).
When estimating Singapore GST on USD ad spend, **convert the spend to SGD first**, then apply 9% (2026).
Treating USD 100k as S$100k **understates the taxable base** (the amount the tax is charged on) (2026).
Ad spend in some other countries carries **VAT rates higher** than Singapore's 9% GST (2026).

The total tax on scaling spend (growing ad spending) must be **included in the budget** (2026).
Ads taxes in the UK and EU were flagged as a risk (undated).
Sales tax obligations for ad spend are **not separate from nexus**.

p.t: **Identify your home state**, check its sales tax rules, and register there before charging tax (2024),.

Sales tax nexus is typically triggered at around **$100,000 in sales per year per state**.
Collect sales tax only where you have nexus.

Avoid collecting or paying it in states where you have none.
Sales tax applies in the state where the business is registered if that state has sales tax.

This applies to orders shipped to addresses in that state.
Not every US state has sales tax.
For most states, **economic nexus (a tax obligation in another state) starts when sales in that state exceed 100,000 dollars** in a year.
Check each state's rules with an accountant.
Before any state reaches its economic nexus threshold, a store charges sales tax **only on orders shipping to the state where it is registered** and holds a sales tax certificate.
Each other state is added **only when the store reaches that state's threshold**.
